prompt:
Generate one high-quality cinematic 16:9 image for the specified section, not a generic slide or dashboard. No letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, arrows, diagrams, interface, checkmarks, traffic-light statuses or readable documents. The compositor adds every semantic mark independently. Do not invent a completed publication, a live security test, a solved outing, approval or consensus. Fictional editorial staging, not documentary evidence. Rich material detail, carefully controlled light, credible objects and hands. Keep designated annotation zones visually quiet. Never fill quiet zones with invented panels. Reference images establish cast and room identity only; follow this section's camera and blocking.
VISUAL FORMAT: completion-report-redline
TEACHING PURPOSE: Make the unsupported success claim disappear while supported facts remain.
CAMERA: Close overhead editorial desk, paper fills the frame asymmetrically.
A completely blank cream report sheet lies diagonally across a charcoal editorial desk, occupying the CENTRAL TWO THIRDS. A red pencil rests beside its upper-right edge, untouched. A second smaller blank paper sits at the far left. Directional warm light reveals paper grain, a narrow shadow under the sheet, no handwriting or printing, no red marks, stamps or checkmarks. Plenty of uninterrupted paper for precise SVG redlining and a corrected agent report. No hand signs or approves anything.
COMPOSITING INTENT: Large report sentence across the page receives a deliberate redline; the truthful replacement is written beneath in a different typographic hierarchy.
SEMANTIC AUTHORITY FOR CONTEXT ONLY, NEVER RENDER THESE WORDS: REPORT REVIEW / FICTIONAL. Compare the reports. Outing arranged, everyone can attend: unsupported. Replace it with: room reserved; two members report a travel conflict; no change authorized. The corrected report preserves the completed action and removes the unsupported conclusion. It also tells the coordinator what remains open.
